speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; can you describe the specific nature of these sensations, such as whether they involve a spinning motion or just a feeling of unsteadiness?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the dizziness is position-dependent and accompanied by a spinning sensation, is this episode associated with any specific head movements like rolling over in bed or turning your head quickly? Also, have you noticed any new hearing loss, ear fullness, or ringing in the affected ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of brief, spinning vertigo strictly triggered by head position changes, combined with age and a history of hearing loss without new neurological deficits, is highly characteristic of BPPV.
